## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kammakathā* ("Discussion of Deeds") is the seventh treatise of the first division (*Mahāvagga*) of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* [Frauwallner 1995]. In his overview of early Abhidharma literature, Erich Frauwallner evaluated the *Kammakathā* (I, 7)—along with the *Abhisamayakathā* (III, 3)—as an isolated attempt within the scholastic tradition to treat a doctrinal problem independently, though he critically observed that such treatments showed little development beyond pedantic elaboration and suggested an Abhidharma tradition that was "silting up and dessicating" [Frauwallner 1995].

**Sources**

- [Frauwallner 1995] Erich Frauwallner, Studies in Abhidharma Literature and the Origins of Buddhist Philosophical System (1995) — Discussed the independent topical nature and scholastic character of the Kammakathā (I, 7).
